quote: Churn means no spend in the 60 days after the snapshot. It reports: 'Churn by snapshot month: 11, 12, 11, 12, 6 and 2 percent.'
explanation: The question pairs the course's inactivity definition ('no spend in the 60 days after the snapshot') and 'one snapshot per month' with a pattern ('6 and 2 percent') and explanation ('advertisers who will still leave are sitting in the stayed column') that only hold for point-in-time events like account cancellations. Under 'no spend at all in the 60 days after the snapshot', any advertiser who has already spent since the snapshot has positive 60-day spend and can never become a churner for that snapshot even if they stop later. Meanwhile, querying spend == 0 on an unclosed window makes recent churn spike upward (every true 60-day churner has zero spend so far, plus temporary pausers have zero spend so far), and defaulting unclosed monthly snapshots to stayed would produce 0% for an entire unclosed snapshot date, not 6% and 2%.

quote: An advertiser whose snapshot was 20 days ago has not survived 60 days. They have survived 20. Label them as stayed, and you have filed some future churners under loyal.
explanation: This contradicts the 60-day zero-spend definition just taught in the predict question and seg1 ('no spend at all in the 60 days after a snapshot date'). quote: Label them as stayed, and you have filed some future churners under loyal.
problem: The lesson treats the churn label as an event that accrues over the window ('has not survived 60 days', 'some of them will still churn'), but the course's label is an absence: churned = no spend at all in the 60 days, and one spend anywhere in the window settles the row as stayed (the lesson's own guess-first answer). For that label an open window errs the other way when computed literally (SUM of spend in the window = 0): everyone who has not spent yet is counted as churned, so recent months come out too HIGH, and an advertiser who has already spent is a confirmed stayer who cannot 'still churn'. The 6 and 2 percent collapse in 1-3-q1 arises only for an event-type label or an 'inactive for 60 days so far' implementation, which the question does not state. A learner taught 'open window = suspiciously low' will read an inflated recent churn rate as a real rise.
